description: The Phase 6 lean conversational baseline turn set. THIS FILE IS AUTHORITATIVE. The protocol document describes the set; the JS route preflight routes these exact strings through the shipped browser router; the Python capture requires these exact narrator inputs in this exact order and refuses anything else. Three consumers, one list.

scoring.quality_aggregate: Membership is MEASURED, not declared. A turn belongs to the generated-Lori aggregate when its trace records generation_attempted=true. The first run proved why: turn 6 was declared out of the aggregate on the assumption that the browser's 'correction' route made it deterministic, and it generated anyway.
scoring.requested_vs_effective: The browser router (app.js lvRouteTurn) decides the REQUESTED mode. The server may reset it: chat_ws.py:5031 resets both copies to 'interview' when parse_correction_rule_based() finds no actionable target or value. A trace showing effective_turn_mode='interview' therefore does NOT prove the browser sent 'interview'. The preflight checks the requested route only; the trace records requested_turn_mode, effective_turn_mode and generation_attempted as three separate facts.
scoring.turn_6: Kept in the baseline. It additionally answers whether the correction path handles a genuine self-correction and hands continuity back — but if it generated, it is also ordinary conversational evidence.

turns.text: My brother Dennis used to walk me to school through the cemetery because it was the fast way.
We left Currier Street the summer I turned eleven and moved out toward Websterville.
These days I'm up before Warren. I make the coffee and do the crossword while the house is quiet.
At the practice I ended up building the schedule for both dentists. Nobody ever asked me to. I just started doing it.
My father came home from the quarry one afternoon and told us his hands had stopped working right. He was fifty-two.
Actually, he was fifty-four, not fifty-two. I keep getting that wrong.
Claire moved out to California the same year we lost the house on Berlin Street.
There was a green glass dish on the hall table. I have no idea why I remember it.
We used to drive up to Groton Pond on Sundays in the summer, all four of us in the wagon.
I couldn't tell you what year we got the camp. Somewhere in the seventies.

hazard_witness.why: The ten turns above are worded AROUND the browser correction detector at ui/js/app.js:2600, which fires on ordinary narration. CORRECTED 2026-09-07: an earlier version of this note said such sentences 'would never reach the model'. That is not established. The browser sets the REQUESTED mode; chat_ws.py:5031 resets it to interview when parse_correction_rule_based() finds nothing actionable, and the turn then generates normally. What the detector reliably does is route the turn through the correction branch first, where an actionable parse WOULD produce a deterministic acknowledgement instead of a conversation. Recorded as a Phase 6 defect-list item. We word around it ONLY for this first baseline; real future conversations must not be shaped by a regex.
sentences: There was a green glass dish on the hall table. I do not know why I remember it, not that it matters.
It was not a big house, but we managed.
It wasn't the same after that.
hazard_witness.control: We used to drive up to Groton Pond on Sundays.
